questions.q: What term matches this definition: The smallest, fundamental unit of ordinary matter that forms chemical elements.
What term matches this definition: A substance consisting of atoms which all have the same number of protons; neutral overall charge.
What term matches this definition: An atom or molecule with a net electric charge due to loss or gain of electrons.
What term matches this definition: A positively charged ion (loses electrons).
What term matches this definition: A negatively charged ion (gains electrons).
What term matches this definition: A compound made of metal cations and non-metal anions held together by ionic bonds.
What term matches this definition: The force that attracts oppositely charged particles (ions) and repels like charges.
What term matches this definition: Strong electrostatic attraction between oppositely charged ions formed by electron transfer.
What term matches this definition: An ordered, repeating three-dimensional arrangement of ions in an ionic compound.
What term matches this definition: A compound made of metal cations surrounded by a 'sea' of delocalised electrons.
What term matches this definition: Electrostatic attraction between metal cations and delocalised electrons.
What term matches this definition: Bonds where attraction extends uniformly in all directions, e.g., ionic and metallic bonds.
What term matches this definition: A compound made of molecules held together by covalent bonds and intermolecular forces.
What term matches this definition: Intramolecular bond formed by sharing pairs of valence electrons between atoms.
What term matches this definition: Weak forces of attraction between molecules, including temporary dipoles, permanent dipoles, and hydrogen bonding.
What term matches this definition: A pair of valence electrons not involved in bonding (non-bonding electrons).
What term matches this definition: Chemical principle that atoms tend to bond to have eight electrons in their valence shell for stability.
What term matches this definition: A 2D representation showing valence electrons as dots and covalent bonds as lines.
What term matches this definition: Valence Shell Electron Pair Repulsion theory predicting 3D molecular shapes by repulsion of electron pairs.
What term matches this definition: Organic compounds made only of carbon and hydrogen atoms.
What term matches this definition: Saturated hydrocarbon with only single bonds; general formula CₙH₂ₙ₊₂.
What term matches this definition: Unsaturated hydrocarbon with at least one carbon-carbon double bond; general formula CₙH₂ₙ.
What term matches this definition: Unsaturated hydrocarbon with at least one carbon-carbon triple bond; general formula CₙH₂ₙ₋₂.
What term matches this definition: Specific group of atoms responsible for characteristic reactions of a compound (e.g., -OH in alcohols).
What term matches this definition: Part of the name indicating the number of carbon atoms in the main chain (meth-, eth-, prop-, etc.).
What term matches this definition: Part of the name indicating the type of hydrocarbon or functional group (-ane, -ene, -yne, -ol).
What term matches this definition: Hydrocarbon branch attached to the main carbon chain but not part of it (e.g., methyl, ethyl).
What term matches this definition: Shows the exact number and types of atoms in a molecule (e.g., C₆H₁₄).
What term matches this definition: Graphic representation showing how atoms are bonded in a molecule.
What term matches this definition: Shorthand notation listing atoms in order bonded, grouping hydrogens next to carbons.
What term matches this definition: Simplified organic formula where carbon atoms are vertices/ends of lines and hydrogens are implied.
What term matches this definition: Compounds with the same molecular formula but different connectivity of atoms.
What term matches this definition: Ring-shaped hydrocarbons with alternating single and double bonds (e.g., benzene).
What term matches this definition: Process of breaking long-chain hydrocarbons into shorter, more useful molecules using heat and catalysts.
What term matches this definition: Separation technique that separates mixtures based on different boiling points.
What term matches this definition: Laboratory technique to heat reactions at constant temperature without loss of solvent by condensation.
What term matches this definition: Refers to the number of hydrogens attached to carbons; saturated hydrocarbons have maximum hydrogens.
What term matches this definition: Reaction where atoms or groups are added to an unsaturated molecule, breaking double or triple bonds.
What term matches this definition: Reaction where atoms or groups are removed from a molecule, forming double bonds.
What term matches this definition: In addition reactions, the hydrogen attaches to the carbon with more hydrogens already attached.
What term matches this definition: In elimination reactions, the double bond forms at the carbon with fewer hydrogens (least saturated).
What term matches this definition: Organic compounds containing carbon, hydrogen, and at least one halogen atom (F, Cl, Br, I).
What term matches this definition: Organic compounds with at least one hydroxyl (-OH) group attached to a carbon.
What term matches this definition: Organic compounds containing a carboxyl group (-COOH).
What term matches this definition: Exothermic reaction where a fuel reacts with oxygen to produce carbon dioxide, water, and energy.
What term matches this definition: Heat content of a system; change in enthalpy is heat absorbed or released during a reaction.
What term matches this definition: Reaction that releases heat; ΔH is negative.
What term matches this definition: Combustion with sufficient oxygen producing CO₂ and H₂O.
What term matches this definition: Combustion with limited oxygen producing CO, C (soot), and H₂O.
